exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Sum of Vectors Using the Pythagorean Theorem

question.text: Consider the diagram above, where $\mathbf{a}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$, $|\mathbf{a}|=12$ and $|\mathbf{b}|=9.$ Find the exact value of $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
Notice that we have a right triangle. So, we can use Pythagorean theorem as follows:

\begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[3pt] &={12}^2+{9}^2 \\[3pt] &=144+81\\[5pt] & =225 \end{align*}

Hence, $|\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{225}= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{15}.$

question.text: Consider the diagram above, where $\mathbf{a}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$, $|\mathbf{a}|=4$ and $|\mathbf{b}|=7.$ Find the exact value of $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
Notice that we have a right triangle. So, we can use Pythagorean theorem as follows:

\begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[3pt] &={4}^2+{7}^2 \\[3pt] &=65 \end{align*}

Hence, $|\mathbf{a+b}|= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\sqrt{65}}.$

example.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Sum of Vectors Using the Pythagorean Theorem

question.explanation:
As we can see from the picture above, in $\bigtriangleup BAD$ we have $\angle BAD=90^\circ$, $AB=18$ and $AD=BC=9.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

\begin{align*} |\overrightarrow{BD}| &= BD \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{AB^2+AD^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{18^2+9^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{405} \\[5pt] &= 9\sqrt 5. \end{align*}

Hence, $|\overrightarrow{BD}|=9\sqrt 5.$

example.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Sum of Vectors Using the Pythagorean Theorem

question.text: In rectangle $ABCD,$ $AB=10$ and $BC=6\sqrt{2}.$ Find the exact value of $|\overrightarrow{BD}|.$
question.explanation:
As we can see from the picture above, in $\bigtriangleup BAD$ we have $m\angle{BAD} = 90^\circ,$ $AB=10,$ and $AD = BC = 6\sqrt{2}.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives \begin{align*} |\overrightarrow{BD}| &= BD \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{AB^2+AD^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{10^2 + \big(6\sqrt{2}\big)^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{100 + 72} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{172} \\[5pt] &= 2\sqrt{43}. \end{align*}

Hence, $|\overrightarrow{BD}|=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2\sqrt{43}}.$
